---
title: "Score an Analysis against a simulation"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

On simulated data the true transmission network is known, so you can measure how well plasmotrack recovers it. This
article shows you how to read a simulation's truth, score the edges, Parent sets, genotypes, and COI of an Analysis
against it, summarise a fit in one row with `pt_fit_summary()`, and score many simulations at once as a job array on a
SLURM cluster.

The article uses the example simulation from `pt_example()`: four Runs of the full model, one Run of the null model,
and the simulator's truth.

## Before you begin

Load the packages and download the example:

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(plasmotrackr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

ex <- pt_example()
a <- pt_read(ex$full, input = ex$input)
```

Before you score a fit, check that its Runs agree. For more information, see
[Check convergence across Runs](convergence.html).

## Read the truth

`pt_read_truth()` reads the simulator's JSON output, gzipped or not. The result holds the true edges, the
Infections with their true infection and observation times, the true genotype of every strain, the Loci, and each
case's observed genotype:

```{r truth}
truth <- pt_read_truth(ex$truth)
truth
truth$edges
```

The truth covers every case of the simulated outbreak, observed or not. Scoring restricts it to the Infections of
the Analysis, so one truth serves every fit of a simulation, such as a fit to all cases and a fit to a subsample.
Ids are strings in both.

In a fit to a subsample, not every case is observed, and the share of true edges with both ends observed bounds what
any fit can recover. This example fits every case, so the share is 1:

```{r observed-edges}
observed <- pt_infections(a)$infection
truth$edges |>
  summarise(
    true_edges = n(),
    both_observed = sum(parent %in% observed & child %in% observed)
  )
```

## Score the edges

`pt_score_edges()` ranks every ordered pair of Infections by its pooled Edge marginal and scores the ranking against
the true edges. It returns one row for directed edges and one for undirected edges, where a pair's score is the sum
of both directions:

```{r score-edges}
pt_score_edges(a, truth)
```

The columns are the following:

- `n_edge_universe`: the number of pairs ranked.
- `n_true_edges`: the number of true edges among them.
- `average_precision` and `pr_auc`: two summaries of the precision-recall curve.
- `top_k_precision`: the precision among the *k* highest-scoring pairs, where *k* is the number of true edges.

A true edge whose parent was never observed cannot be recovered directly. With `edges = "transitive"`, a pair also
counts as true when a path through unobserved cases only joins the two Infections. This example observes every case, so
the table matches the one above; the option matters for fits to a subsample:

```{r score-edges-transitive}
pt_score_edges(a, truth, edges = "transitive")
```

Set `curve = TRUE` for the precision-recall curve itself:

```{r pr-curve}
pt_score_edges(a, truth, curve = TRUE) |>
  ggplot(aes(recall, precision, colour = direction)) +
  geom_step(direction = "vh") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))
```

## Score the Parent sets

An Infection's true Parent set is its true parents among the observed Infections, plus the Latent parent when the
Infection is a root of the outbreak or has a true parent that was not observed.

`pt_score_parent_sets()` checks, for each Infection, whether the true Parent set is in its Credible collection: the
highest-ranked Parent sets that hold 80% of the posterior weight. Coverage near 0.8 with small collections is the
goal:

```{r score-parent-sets}
sets <- pt_score_parent_sets(a, truth)
sets |>
  summarise(
    coverage = mean(covered),
    mean_credible_size = mean(credible_size),
    mean_top_probability = mean(top_probability)
  )
```

`pt_score_map()` checks whether each Infection's MAP Parent set, its single most probable set, is the true one:

```{r score-map}
map <- pt_score_map(a, truth)
mean(map$correct)
```

List the Infections whose MAP Parent set is wrong, with the true set next to it:

```{r score-map-wrong}
map |>
  filter(!correct) |>
  select(infection, members, has_latent_parent, weight, true_members, true_has_latent_parent)
```

## Score the Functionals

A Functional is one number per Draw, such as the mean out-degree. Compare its posterior interval with the value of
the same Functional on the true network. The true mean out-degree counts the true edges between observed Infections:

```{r functional-truth}
true_mean_out_degree <- truth$edges |>
  filter(parent %in% observed, child %in% observed) |>
  nrow() / length(observed)

pt_mean_out_degree(a) |>
  pt_interval() |>
  pt_plot_interval(truth = true_mean_out_degree)
```

## Score the genotypes and COI

plasmotrack infers each Infection's genotype at every Locus. `pt_score_genotypes()` calls an Allele present when its
posterior presence is at least 0.5 and compares the calls with the true Alleles:

```{r score-genotypes}
genotypes <- pt_score_genotypes(a, truth)
genotypes |>
  summarise(
    exact = mean(exact),
    true_positives = sum(true_positives),
    false_positives = sum(false_positives),
    false_negatives = sum(false_negatives),
    unrepresentable = sum(unrepresentable)
  )
```

A true Allele that no observed Infection shows cannot be inferred; it is counted as `unrepresentable` and left out of
the other counts.

The posterior presence of each Allele is in `pt_genotype_presence()`. Plot it for a few Infections, with one panel per
Locus:

```{r genotype-plot, fig.height = 6}
first_infections <- head(sort(observed), 6)
pt_genotype_presence(a) |>
  filter(infection %in% first_infections) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(allele), infection, fill = presence)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(vars(locus), scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Allele", y = "Infection")
```

`pt_score_coi()` compares each Infection's posterior median COI with its true COI, counted as the most distinct true
genotypes at any observed Locus:

```{r score-coi}
coi <- pt_score_coi(a, truth)
count(coi, true_coi, median)
```

The posterior distribution of each Infection's COI is in `pt_coi()`, as the list column `distribution`. The following
helper unnests it:

```{r tidy-coi}
tidy_coi <- function(x) {
  bind_rows(Map(function(id, d) mutate(d, infection = id), x$infection, x$distribution))
}
```

Plot the distribution for the 12 Infections whose COI is least certain, with the true COI as a dashed line:

```{r coi-plot}
coi_distribution <- tidy_coi(pt_coi(a))
least_certain <- coi_distribution |>
  group_by(infection) |>
  summarise(top_fraction = max(fraction)) |>
  slice_min(top_fraction, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE)

coi_distribution |>
  filter(infection %in% least_certain$infection) |>
  left_join(select(coi, infection, true_coi), by = "infection") |>
  ggplot(aes(coi, fraction)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = true_coi), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(vars(infection)) +
  labs(x = "COI", y = "Posterior probability")
```

## Summarise a fit in one row

`pt_fit_summary()` computes every score above, and posterior intervals of the Functionals, as one row with 70
columns. Rows of different fits bind into one table:

```{r fit-summary}
full_row <- pt_fit_summary(a, truth)
full_row |>
  select(
    fit_type, n_true_cases, n_observed_cases, true_average_outdegree, estimated_average_outdegree,
    directed_average_precision, credible_parent_set_coverage_80
  )
```

The first 12 columns describe the simulation, such as its size and genetic panel. They are `NA` unless you pass a
one-row data frame as `factors`.

The null model ignores the observed genotypes and observation times, so its Run samples the prior. It gives the
baseline that the full model must beat: a score no better than the null model's comes from the prior, not the data. Open it as its own Analysis, because
`pt_read()` doesn't mix full-model and null-model Runs, and set `fit_type = "null_prior"`:

```{r null-model}
null <- pt_read(ex$null, input = ex$input)
null_row <- pt_fit_summary(null, truth, fit_type = "null_prior")

bind_rows(full_row, null_row) |>
  select(fit_type, estimated_unobserved_source_proportion, directed_average_precision, mean_top_parent_set_probability)
```

In the fit summary, the Latent parent probability is named the unobserved source proportion.

### Optional: score pairwise relatedness

Pairwise relatedness estimates, such as identity by descent (IBD) between two Infections, rank pairs without a
direction. `pt_score_pairs()` scores a data frame of `a`, `b`, and `score` against the true edges. The example holds
no such estimates, so the following code doesn't run here:

```{r score-pairs, eval = FALSE}
ibd <- read.csv("ibd.csv", colClasses = c(a = "character", b = "character"))
pt_score_pairs(ibd, truth, infections = observed)
```

With `fit_type = "dcifer"` and `scores = ibd`, `pt_fit_summary()` puts the same scores in the fit-summary layout.

## Score many simulations as a job array

A simulation study scores hundreds of fits. plasmotrackr has no cohort function: you loop over your directory layout
and bind the rows. On a SLURM cluster, run the loop as a job array, one simulation per task, with each task writing
a one-row file.

The following layout is an example. Each simulation has its own directory with its truth, its input, and its Runs:

```
simulations/
  sim_001/
    truth.json.gz
    input.json.gz
    full/run1/ ... full/run4/
    null/run1/
  sim_002/
  ...
```

### Write the scoring script

Save the following script as `score-one.R`. It reads the task index from `SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`, scores the matching
simulation, and saves its two rows:

```{r score-one, eval = FALSE}
library(plasmotrackr)

simulations <- sort(list.dirs("simulations", recursive = FALSE))
task <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID"))
sim <- simulations[task]
threads <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "1"))

truth <- pt_read_truth(file.path(sim, "truth.json.gz"))
input <- file.path(sim, "input.json.gz")
factors <- data.frame(simulation = basename(sim))

full <- pt_read(file.path(sim, "full"), input = input, threads = threads, memory_limit = "6GB")
null <- pt_read(file.path(sim, "null"), input = input, threads = threads, memory_limit = "6GB")
rows <- rbind(
  pt_fit_summary(full, truth, factors = factors),
  pt_fit_summary(null, truth, fit_type = "null_prior", factors = factors)
)

dir.create("scores", showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(rows, file.path("scores", paste0(basename(sim), ".rds")))
```

Set `memory_limit` below the memory that you request for each task. DuckDB spills to `temp_directory` beyond it,
which defaults to R's temporary directory; on a cluster, point it at node-local scratch space if your site has it.

### Submit the array

Save the following batch script as `score.sbatch`. Set `--array` to the number of simulations, and replace the
module line with however your cluster provides R:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=score
#SBATCH --array=1-200%50
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/score-%A_%a.out

module load r
Rscript score-one.R
```

The `%50` suffix runs at most 50 tasks at once. Create the `logs` directory, then submit the script from the
directory that holds `simulations/`:

```bash
mkdir -p logs
sbatch score.sbatch
```

Install plasmotrackr into your user library before you submit. If compute nodes have no internet access, install it
on a login node.

### Bind the rows

After every task finishes, bind the rows into one table:

```{r bind-rows, eval = FALSE}
scores <- list.files("scores", pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  lapply(readRDS) |>
  bind_rows()
```

A task that failed leaves no file. Compare the files with the simulation directories to find the tasks to rerun.

```{r close, include = FALSE}
pt_close(a)
pt_close(null)
```
